_meta.purpose: Common ML mistakes in financial ML and their fixes

anti_patterns.wrong: Fixed pip TP/SL (e.g., TP=50 pips, SL=50 pips)
anti_patterns.why: Fixed pip ignores volatility regime — over-labels in calm markets, under-labels in volatile

anti_patterns.right: Meta-labeling for take/skip (0/1) given direction from primary
anti_patterns.why: Meta-label is binary 0/1 — cannot express direction. Side MUST come from primary model or CUSUM
Prado: 'PT > SL gives the signal more room to be right'. Symmetric → ~50/50 → random
Standard KFold leaks: train labels overlap test period → inflated OOS metrics

anti_patterns.right: DF_Curve, Flow_Delta, PV_Corr, Mom_Persistence, Vol_Adj_Mom, VR_1_4
anti_patterns.why: RSI/ADX/Stochastic AUC≈0.53 for direction — barely better than random. They measure magnitude, not direction

anti_patterns.right: Returns, log-returns, or fractionally differenced prices
anti_patterns.why: Raw price non-stationary → model learns price level, not dynamics
Time bars oversample in volatile periods → heteroscedastic → poor ML performance
Overlapping triple barriers create concurrent labels → unweighted = biased toward overlaps

anti_patterns.right: Mix boolean + float — trees split better on boolean
anti_patterns.why: AlphaPy: boolean features enable context combinations (e.g., CUSUM_Down & RSI_Oversold)

anti_patterns.wrong: Feature uses close[t] for prediction at t (no shift)
anti_patterns.right: All features use .shift(1) — only data up to t-1
anti_patterns.why: Using close[t] is lookahead bias → leakage → inflated OOS → production failure

anti_patterns.wrong: Same threshold for long and short (e.g., 0.5)
anti_patterns.why: Shorts are riskier → need higher confidence threshold
Each instrument has different vol, tick size, dollar threshold — hardcoding = bugs

anti_patterns.wrong: FVG detection without ATR size filter
anti_patterns.why: Without ATR filter, tiny gaps in choppy markets create noise features — too many false FVGs

anti_patterns.wrong: Volume Profile POC requires footprint/tick data
anti_patterns.right: Approximate POC from OHLC bar volume — distribute bar volume centered at close price
anti_patterns.why: BTCUSD/XAUUSD have no footprint data — but OHLC+V proxy is effective for POC detection
anti_patterns.reference: advisors/nq1_Scalping_Strategy — Volume Profile from bar data

anti_patterns.wrong: Emitting signal on every bar where condition holds
anti_patterns.right: Fresh Trigger: signal only on FIRST bar of new condition + cooldown period
anti_patterns.why: Without Fresh Trigger, model generates 10+ identical signals in a trending move → overtrading

anti_patterns.wrong: Single complex model for both direction and sizing
anti_patterns.right: Meta-labeling pipeline: primary model for SIDE, secondary for SIZE (take/skip)
anti_patterns.why: One model cannot optimize both direction accuracy and position sizing simultaneously — meta-labeling separates concerns
anti_patterns.reference: MlFinLab AFML Ch.3 + advisors/EA31337 ensemble approach

anti_patterns.wrong: No time-of-day / session filter — trading all hours equally
anti_patterns.right: Kill Zone filter + session_vol_rank: only trade in high-vol sessions (London/NY open)
anti_patterns.why: Asian session has 3-5x less volume — signals in low-vol hours have much lower win rate

anti_patterns.title: Post-trade judge (Narrator vs Trader)
anti_patterns.description: Training a model on realized trade outcomes (exit price, P&L, MFE/MAE) to rate trades. The answer is already in the inputs — look-ahead bias. The model can never make money because at decision time those inputs don't exist.
anti_patterns.wrong_approach: Give model the realized outcome and ask it to classify good/bad trades
anti_patterns.correct_approach: Meta-labeling: secondary model decides take/skip using ONLY pre-entry information. Features from df[df.index < entry_ts], label is the forward return.
anti_patterns.detection: Any feature that references trade exit, P&L, or outcome is look-ahead

anti_patterns.title: Single-split validation flattery
anti_patterns.description: Reporting results from a single held-out split. Looks great on noise (Sharpe 1.8 on random data) but collapses under purged walk-forward CV. The honest result is often that apparent profit is mostly market exposure, not skill.
anti_patterns.wrong_approach: Train/test single split, report test metrics
anti_patterns.correct_approach: Purged + embargoed walk-forward CV. Benchmark against buy-and-hold beta. Report how many folds beat beta. A verdict that can say NO.
anti_patterns.detection: If no cross-validation or only k-fold (not walk-forward), result is unreliable
